author: Bodostock
text:
Hi, this is my first posting on QM. I have some queries to ask, hope to get some lights.

The chart shown is the EURUSD H4 timeframe, the current price is now near to the monthly and weekly support zone.

Questions: 1. Did i indicate my L, H, LL, HH, Qm correctly? I actually have doubts on their positions.

2. After the LL, am i right to say that supply has been engulfed by demand and then formed the FTR as per indicated? I stated the green portion as FTR because after the supply has been consumed, it retraced to that level and from there, price reversed higher and cleared the next supply zone "H" and formed the "HH".

3. After the "HH", it retraced back down again to the FTR. Do we consider that as a FTB? Also is it also a QM?

4. The reasons why i have my doubts about L, H, LL, HH areas are because when i changed the chart to daily time frame, it seems to tell me that the correct area should be as per below. And if switching back to H4 using these new positions, we can see that they are now at different level where these points are not just consists of a few candles or cap but rather each of them consists of a base zone as per the new chart shown. So which one is correct?

5. With regards to the QM position, i would like to ask which level should it really move to after the HH to consider as QM? Is it a must that after the HH, price must return back to the same level of the "L" but not beyond it so as to qualify as a QM? When i was reading the postings under the thread " Homework - Quasimodo", i read the posting #19 by Master trader whiteout on page 1 that " well, generally speaking i am more picky whit qm,..to the pip? obviously not, but you see that the L is clearly broken, is the reaction around that level that make a QM a QM, otherways is something else.....". It was then i realised about this point and started looking back again on the charts posted by others on page 1 and noticed that indeed most QM retraced back to the "L" but not beyond. But then there were a few charts showing QM lower than the "L" level but rebounded at the origin of the move at LL. One example is the chart posted by IF on page 1 posting #20. As such, do i deemed that the QM level can be either at the DP of L or even back to the top/bottom aka the point of origin after the HH? And whether it is going to form at the "L" level or going beyond to reach the point of origin, we have to observe the reaction it gives at level " L"?
